findings.title: Duplicate downsize definition silently removes the existing width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading: defining `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the earlier `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. Any existing caller using the old signature, e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, temp, 100, 100, opts)`, will now raise ArgumentError. A four-positional call passing width and height will be interpreted as width plus opts and fail when the code reads `opts[:allow_animation]`. The old public method is no longer usable, so this needs to be a distinct method name or a single method that accepts both forms.

findings.title: Downsize loop can proceed with a file still over the limit and ignores failed conversions
findings.body: The loop makes at most five 80% resize attempts, then calls `Upload.create_for` without checking `tempfile.size` again against `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. If five attempts are not enough, the new guard has not actually enforced the limit and the oversized file proceeds to upload. The loop also ignores the boolean result of `OptimizedImage.downsize`, so a failed conversion still consumes an attempt and leaves the original size unchanged. The code needs a post-loop size check and an explicit abort/error path when conversion fails or the file remains too large.

findings.title: Hard-coded 10 MB no longer honors configured attachment size limits
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` is used for both images and attachments, but the new code replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a fixed `10 * 1024` KB. For attachments this bypasses `max_attachment_size_kb`: files up to 10 MB are allowed client-side even when the site limit is lower, and files larger than 10 MB are rejected even when the site setting allows them. The 413 handler at line 246 repeats the same hard-coded assumption and can display the wrong limit.

findings.title: Animated GIF detection uses the temp path, so uploaded animations can be flattened
findings.body: The new call passes `tempfile.path` as the source to `OptimizedImage.downsize`. `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the animated branch only when the source path matches `/\.GIF$/i`, but Rack multipart temp files normally do not carry the original uploaded extension. As a result, `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is ineffective for normal uploads and animated GIFs are handled by the static `downsize_instructions`, whose `convert ... #{from}[0]` keeps only the first frame. Animated uploads can silently become static images.

findings.title: Remote URL downloads now ignore configured size limits for all upload types
findings.body: Changing `FileHelper.download` from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to `10.megabytes` applies to every URL upload, including non-images. A site with a smaller `max_attachment_size_kb` or `max_image_size_kb` will now fetch up to 10 MB from the remote URL before validation, increasing resource use and bypassing the configured limit. If larger images are intended only so they can be auto-downsized, the download limit should be conditional on the upload type or based on an explicit setting.

findings.title: No tests cover the new auto-downsize path
findings.body: The PR changes upload size enforcement, overwrites uploaded image files, and relies on method dispatch inside `OptimizedImage`, but adds no tests for oversized static images, animated GIFs, failed conversions, non-image uploads, or the five-attempt cap. Regressions such as the duplicate `downsize` method or the animation branch being skipped would not be caught.
